# Every query on a table that carries a firm_id which the guard cannot see scoped, and why that is all right.
# Read tests/test_every_query_on_a_firm_table_carries_its_firm_scope.py before touching this file.
#
#   file | function | table | operation | chains | category | note
#
# `table` is a real table, `<dynamic>` (named by a variable), `repo:<singleton>.<method>` or
# `call:<function>` (a CALL the guard reads as the query it stands for). `chains` is how many
# chains share the key; the figure is an EXACT equality in both directions, so a fix that
# removes a chain must remove its line in the same commit, and a new unscoped chain fails
# until somebody writes down why it is fine. `category` is one of the guard's CATEGORIES and
# the note carries what that category's check reads (`route=`, `gate=`, `lookup=`, `source=`,
# `token=`, `signature=`, `symbol=`, `via=`).
#
# Sorted by (file, function, table, operation).
